scenes.tts: A longer neurite grows faster. Is that enough to make one winner?
scenes.visual: Title card: What Makes a Winner. Five bars of slightly different height.
scenes.narration: A longer neurite grows faster. Is that enough to make one winner?

scenes.tts: Here is a model, not a measurement.
scenes.visual: Label in the corner for the whole chapter: illustrative model.
scenes.narration: Here is a model, not a measurement.

scenes.tts: Start with five neurites. Four are fifteen micrometres long, and one is twenty, five micrometres ahead.
scenes.caption: Start with five neurites. Four are 15 micrometres long, and one is 20, 5 micrometres ahead.
scenes.visual: Five bars: four at 15 micrometres, one at 20. Numbers on screen.
scenes.narration: Start with five neurites. Four are 15 micrometres long, and one is 20, 5 micrometres ahead.

scenes.tts: Each neurite grows in proportion to its own length. A longer one grows faster.
scenes.visual: On screen: growth in proportion to length.
scenes.narration: Each neurite grows in proportion to its own length. A longer one grows faster.

scenes.tts: Run the rule for two days. Does one neurite win?
scenes.visual: A clock set to 48 hours; question on screen.
scenes.narration: Run the rule for two days. Does one neurite win?

scenes.tts: No. All five grow. The leader stays the same fraction ahead, a third longer than each sibling.
scenes.visual: All five bars rise together. On screen: leader : next = 1.33, frozen.
scenes.narration: No. All five grow. The leader stays the same fraction ahead, a third longer than each sibling.

scenes.tts: The gap in micrometres widens, but nothing holds the others back.
scenes.visual: A bracket between leader and next bar widens; the four bars keep rising.
scenes.narration: The gap in micrometres widens, but nothing holds the others back.

scenes.tts: You end with five long neurites, and no single winner.
scenes.visual: Five tall bars; none gold.
scenes.narration: You end with five long neurites, and no single winner.

scenes.tts: Growing faster the more it grows is true. But growth in simple proportion to length picks no winner.
scenes.visual: Card: proportional growth alone = no winner.
scenes.narration: Growing faster the more it grows is true. But growth in simple proportion to length picks no winner.

scenes.tts: The leader's gain must come at the others' cost. Two ingredients do this.
scenes.visual: Two empty ingredient boxes.
scenes.narration: The leader's gain must come at the others' cost. Two ingredients do this.

scenes.tts: First, positive feedback within a neurite. Growth recruits more of whatever drives growth.
scenes.visual: Box 1 fills: a circular arrow inside one neurite.
scenes.narration: First, positive feedback within a neurite. Growth recruits more of whatever drives growth.

scenes.tts: Second, competition between neurites. One proposal: they draw on a limited supply from the cell body.
scenes.visual: Box 2 fills: a single reservoir in the cell body draining into five pipes; icons flow down them: membrane, tubulin, signalling proteins. Label: one proposal.
scenes.narration: Second, competition between neurites. One proposal: they draw on a limited supply from the cell body.

scenes.tts: So one neurite's gain is the others' loss.
scenes.visual: One pipe widens as the other four narrow.
scenes.narration: So one neurite's gain is the others' loss.

scenes.tts: But even a shared supply is not quite enough.
scenes.visual: Rule two on screen: a shared supply, split in proportion to length.
scenes.narration: But even a shared supply is not quite enough.

scenes.tts: If each neurite takes a share in proportion to its length, the fractions again stay fixed.
scenes.visual: The bars rise again with frozen ratios. On screen: 1.33, unchanged.
scenes.narration: If each neurite takes a share in proportion to its length, the fractions again stay fixed.

scenes.tts: A long neurite's growth, relative to its own length, has to be larger than a short neurite's. There are two ways.
scenes.visual: On screen: growth per unit length must favour the leader.
scenes.narration: A long neurite's growth, relative to its own length, has to be larger than a short neurite's. There are two ways.

scenes.tts: The feedback could be steeper than proportional.
scenes.visual: Rule three: share in proportion to length squared. The leader's bar accelerates.
scenes.narration: The feedback could be steeper than proportional.

scenes.tts: Or every neurite could pay the same fixed running cost, such as retraction.
scenes.visual: Each bar gets a small leak at its base, the same size for all.
scenes.narration: Or every neurite could pay the same fixed running cost, such as retraction.

scenes.tts: That cost takes a bigger bite out of a short neurite's growth.
scenes.visual: The same leak on every bar: a big share of a short bar's growth, a small share of the leader's.
scenes.narration: That cost takes a bigger bite out of a short neurite's growth.

scenes.tts: With either one, a small lead grows into a large one. The others grow about fourfold, then slow to a crawl.
scenes.visual: The leader runs away; four bars rise, then slow to a crawl. On screen: about 5, or about 15.
scenes.narration: With either one, a small lead grows into a large one. The others grow about fourfold, then slow to a crawl.

scenes.tts: With both, the others shrink back to stubs. Now there is one winner.
scenes.visual: Both rules together: the leader turns gold and towers; four bars shrink to a 2 micrometre floor by about 14 hours. On screen: about 400 (about 820 micrometres against the 2 micrometre floor). Model spec in the corner: supply 20 micrometres an hour, cost 2 per neurite, floor 2 micrometres, 48 hours.
scenes.narration: With both, the others shrink back to stubs. Now there is one winner.

scenes.tts: Now place the molecules in the loop.
scenes.visual: A loop diagram appears at one growth cone, with empty slots.
scenes.narration: Now place the molecules in the loop.

scenes.tts: P I three kinase makes the lipid P I P three. It builds up at the tip of the future axon.
scenes.caption: PI3-kinase makes the lipid PIP3. It builds up at the tip of the future axon.
scenes.visual: Slot 1: PI3-kinase makes PIP3 at the tip of the gold neurite.
scenes.narration: PI3-kinase makes the lipid PIP3. It builds up at the tip of the future axon.

scenes.tts: P I P three is a mark at one spot on the membrane. It draws proteins with P H domains to that spot.
scenes.caption: PIP3 is a mark at one spot on the membrane. It draws proteins with PH domains to that spot.
scenes.visual: PIP3 drawn as a bright patch of membrane; proteins with PH domains dock on it.
scenes.narration: PIP3 is a mark at one spot on the membrane. It draws proteins with PH domains to that spot.

scenes.tts: The par complex, which also marks the top of an epithelial cell, gathers there.
scenes.caption: The Par3/Par6/aPKC complex, which also marks the top of an epithelial cell, gathers there.
scenes.visual: Slot 2: the Par3/Par6/aPKC complex, with a small inset of an epithelial cell's top.
scenes.narration: The Par3/Par6/aPKC complex, which also marks the top of an epithelial cell, gathers there.

scenes.tts: At the tip, the switches C D C forty-two and rack reorganize actin.
scenes.caption: At the tip, the switches Cdc42 and Rac reorganize actin.
scenes.visual: Slot 3: Cdc42 and Rac switch on; the actin mesh in the growth cone rearranges.
scenes.narration: At the tip, the switches Cdc42 and Rac reorganize actin.

scenes.tts: Loosened actin is proposed to let microtubules push forward into the growth cone.
scenes.visual: Slot 4: a looser actin net; microtubules push into the growth cone. Label: proposed.
scenes.narration: Loosened actin is proposed to let microtubules push forward into the growth cone.

scenes.tts: Part of the loop is thought to be physical. A faster neurite draws more material and more transport.
scenes.visual: Slot 5: more transport arrives at the gold tip.
scenes.narration: Part of the loop is thought to be physical. A faster neurite draws more material and more transport.

scenes.tts: Then it grows faster still. The loop closes.
scenes.visual: The arrow returns to slot 1; the loop is complete.
scenes.narration: Then it grows faster still. The loop closes.

scenes.tts: There is also a brake. Rho A tends to oppose neurite growth.
scenes.caption: There is also a brake. RhoA tends to oppose neurite growth.
scenes.visual: A brake icon labelled RhoA on the loop.
scenes.narration: There is also a brake. RhoA tends to oppose neurite growth.

scenes.tts: What holds the losers back is less settled. A limited supply and an inhibitory signal are both proposed.
scenes.visual: The four short neurites, with two candidate cards: shared supply; inhibitory signal. Label: proposed.
scenes.narration: What holds the losers back is less settled. A limited supply and an inhibitory signal are both proposed.

scenes.tts: So a winner needs competition, plus something that compounds a lead. Next, can we rig the race?
scenes.visual: Closing card: competition plus a lead that compounds. Next: Rig the Race.
scenes.narration: So a winner needs competition, plus something that compounds a lead. Next, can we rig the race?
